name: Malaysia
change_summary: The base law from 1 October 2025: the EPF Third Schedule Parts A, C, E and F (Parts B and D deleted by Act A1760), SOCSO and EIS on the RM6,000 ceiling, the LMTD 2026 computerised-calculation specification, HRDF, and the Employment Act 1955 as amended by Act A1651 in force 1 January 2023.

limits.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1)(d): not more than 45 hours of work in one week; s.60A(3) pays the hours beyond at one and a half times the hourly rate
Employment (Limitation of Overtime Work) Regulations 1980 reg. 2

work_rules.authority: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule paras 1A, 2 and 3, as substituted by the Employment (Amendment of First Schedule) Order 2022 [P.U. (A) 262], in operation 1 January 2023 — the ladder in ss.60(3), 60A(3), 60D(3) and 60D(4) does not apply to a person whose wages exceed RM4,000 a month, save for the para 2 categories, which are covered irrespective of wages; para 2(4) vessel work is outside Part XII altogether; "wages" is the s.2 definition less commissions, subsistence allowance and overtime payment. The rest break is s.60A(1)(a): an employee shall not be required to work more than five consecutive hours without a period of leisure of not less than thirty minutes; proviso (i) a break of less than thirty minutes does not break the continuity of the five hours, proviso (ii) work that must be carried on continuously may run eight consecutive hours inclusive of not less than forty-five minutes in the aggregate for a meal. The weekly rest day is s.59(1): every employee shall be allowed in each week a rest day of one whole day as determined from time to time by the employer, and where more than one is allowed the LAST is the rest day for the purposes of Part XII; s.59(1A) treats any continuous period of not less than thirty hours as a rest day for shift work. holiday_rest_precedence is SUBSTITUTE on the s.60D(1) proviso: where a gazetted public holiday falls on a rest day, or on another public holiday, the working day next following is a paid holiday in substitution. APPLIED: (a) the s.60A(1)(b)-(d) statement of normal hours — not more than eight hours in one day ("normal_day"), a spread-over of not more than ten hours ("spread_day") and not more than forty-five hours in one week ("weekly_total") — enforced as schedule limits, while every BEYOND_NORMAL band below prices the overtime it derives; Applied 2026-09-18: s.60A(1)(b) the normal day is 8 hours, or up to 9 under the proviso where the contracted week is within 45 (`normal_hours`); s.60A(1)(d) 45 hours a week is a ceiling on normal hours, the hours beyond it overtime (`weekly_normal`, read by payroll), not a wall on the roster; s.60(3)(a) rest-day work of a daily- or hourly-rated employee pays one day’s wages up to half the normal hours and two days’ beyond (`person.terms.pay_frequency`); s.59(1A) the rest day does not run during maternity, sick or hospitalisation leave (`weekly_rest_rule.suspended_by_leave`); First Schedule para 2(5): a domestic employee is outside ss.60–60F and the overtime ladder (`employment.type != "DOMESTIC"`).

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Minimum Wages Order 2024 para 3(2): a domestic employee is outside the Order.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
lom.agc.gov.my — Laws of Malaysia (AGC): every Act and gazette order. The consolidated reprint of a principal Act is /ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act <n>.pdf (452 EPF, 4 SOCSO, 265 Employment, 53 Income Tax; text); an amending Act is a PDF at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/<id>_BI/<Act name>.pdf; a P.U.(A)/(B) order at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/<id>/PUB <n> (<year>).pdf. Use the exact PDF URL listed; the portal search is script-driven and not readable.
kwsp.gov.my — EPF. /en/employer/responsibilities/mandatory-contribution states the Part A/C/E rates, the age gates and the age-75 stop (HTML). /documents/d/guest/third_schedule_from_-1-october-2025 is the Third Schedule download link (the reader gets a shell page; the 1,203-row table is the PDF behind it). /en/employer/responsibilities/non-malaysian-citizen-employees is Part F.
perkeso.gov.my — SOCSO, EIS, SKBBK. /en/rate-of-contribution.html carries the Act 4 / Act 800 tables; /images/lindung/lindung-24-jam/NewContributionRateIncludingSKBBK.pdf is the 65-row table with the SKBBK column (0.2 MB, text); /en/skim-kemalangan-bukan-bencana-kerja-lindung-24-jam.html holds the SKBBK notice and FAQ PDF.
hasil.gov.my — LHDN MTD. /majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data/ lists the yearly "Spesifikasi Kaedah Pengiraan Berkomputer PCB <year>" PDF (/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-<year>.pdf, 1.3 MB, text): Table 1 rates, reliefs, the RM10 minimum.
jtksm.mohr.gov.my — Employment Act 1955 reprint: /sites/default/files/2023-11/Akta Kerja 1955 (Akta 265).pdf (1.4 MB, text): ss.60, 60A, 60D, 60E, 60F, First Schedule. /ms/soalan-lazim/akta-kerja-1955-pindaan-2022 is the 2022 amendment FAQ.
gajiminimum.mohr.gov.my — the Minimum Wages Order in force, as one figure on the landing page.
hrdcorp.gov.my — HRD levy; the site sits behind a browser challenge the reader cannot pass, so note it rather than reading it.
johor.gov.my/rakyat/cuti-umum-2 — the Johor state holiday list for the year.

name: Malaysia — 2026-06-01
change_summary: SKBBK / LINDUNG 24 Jam comes into operation on 1 June 2026: an employee-borne 0.75% contribution (Phase 1) on the SOCSO wage bands and the RM6,000 ceiling, charged in both PERKESO categories. EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB and HRDF are unchanged.

name: Malaysia — 2026-07-08
change_summary: The Cabinet makes SKBBK voluntary for Malaysian citizens and permanent residents with immediate effect on 8 July 2026 (KESUMA confirmed on 9 July; the opt-out window ran 13 July to 31 August). Foreign workers remain mandatory; a local’s Release of Liability is a per-employment NOT_REGISTERED fact.
